You'll gain hands-on experience caring for children from birth to school age, while your formal training is delivered by a registered training organisation (RTO), blending on-the-job learning with structured study.

About the Role
On behalf of our client - a trusted tree care specialist known for precise pruning, safe removals, and expert vegetation management - we are seeking a skilled Tree Worker. You will join a team dedicated to maintaining healthy, safe urban landscapes, working across residential and commercial sites. This role offers variety, from detailed tree assessments to high level climbing and line clearance.

Key Responsibilities & Duties
• Tree Health & Risk Assessment: Examine individual trees to evaluate structural condition, disease, and potential hazards from falling limbs or whole-tree failure; determine appropriate treatment or removal plans.
• Species Selection & Site Planning: Advise on optimal species selection for new plantings, considering local soil conditions, growth patterns, and long-term site management objectives.
• Advanced Climbing & Access: Safely ascend trees using ropes, harnesses, and elevated work platforms (EWPs) to access high limbs and branches for pruning or removal.
• Pruning & Maintenance: Maintain tree and shrub health by pruning limbs and shaping canopies with chainsaws and handsaws to promote strong structure and aesthetic form.
• Hazardous Tree Removal: Remove dead, decaying, or structurally unsound trees, including precision felling and stump grinding to restore site safety.
• Utility Line Clearance: Clear vegetation from overhead electricity and telecommunications lines to prevent outages and fire risks, adhering to strict safety clearances.

Requirements
• Minimum 2 years’ experience as a Tree Worker or Arborist.
• Valid climbing and EWP certifications.
• Competency with chainsaws, handsaws, and stump grinding equipment.
• Knowledge of tree biology, risk assessment, and utility vegetation management.
• Strong safety focus and physical fitness.
• Current driver’s license.

Submit your resume and cover letter via the application portal. We are acting on behalf of our client and will manage all shortlisting.

Role title: Medical Receptionist

Role type: Fixed term 6-month Contract, Full-time (38 hours) - possibility of contract extension

Department and location: St Vincent's Private Hospital Sydney

Salary: $34.51 per hour + Super

Welcome to St Vincent's Private Hospital Sydney, Sydney's premier inner-city private hospital

Join a team built on a proud legacy of world-class care, true compassion, and deep community roots.

Founded in 1857 by the Sisters of Charity and powered today by St Vincent's Health Australia, the Sisters' legacy of compassionate service is our living heartbeat. As a world-class tertiary facility, we are at the forefront of medical innovation, featuring high-acuity interventional suites, next-gen surgical robotics for complex specialties, and cutting-edge oncology backed by the renowned Kinghorn Cancer Centre. Here, you will work alongside global leaders and access funded postgraduate pathways to accelerate your career.

Located in the vibrant heart of Darlinghurst, we are positioned just minutes from Kings Cross station, with direct, high-frequency bus connections from the east, and seamless links from Gadigal and Museum stations right to our doorstep.

We are looking for someone to join us on a 6-month contract (with a possible extension)as aReceptionist in our USpace Facility.

This is a fast-paced position where you will provide administrative support and assistance to clinical teams, patients and their families. To be successful in the role, you will be required to apply your sense of initiative, problem solving ability and professionalism.

About the role

Deliver exceptional front-of-house service by warmly welcoming patients and ensuring a professional, positive experience at every interaction.

Coordinate appointments, respond to patient enquiries, and manage incoming phone calls and email communications efficiently.

Maintain accurate patient records while upholding strict confidentiality and ensuring compliance with privacy standards.

Process billing, payments, and health fund claims accurately, while managing referrals, correspondence, and medical documentation.

Provide comprehensive administrative support to clinicians, contributing to the smooth and efficient day-to-day operation of the practice.

About you

Previous experience in a medical reception or healthcare administration role, with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced clinical environment. Experience with Genie or other medical practice system is desirable.

Exceptional customer service and communication skills, with a compassionate, professional, and patient-focused approach.

Highly organised with excellent attention to detail, strong multitasking abilities, and effective time management skills.

Proficient in Microsoft Office and medical practice management systems such as Genie, Best Practice, Meditech, or Cerner.

Committed to maintaining patient confidentiality and privacy, with a strong understanding of healthcare compliance and professional standards.

What we can offer you

Exceptional Rewards:Competitive pay and not-for-profit salary packaging to maximise your income

For-Purpose Impact: Be part of a not-for-profit where surplus is reinvested into research & community care

World-Class: Collaborate with global leaders across more than 100 medical specialties and 60 service areas

Surgical Innovation: Work with eminent surgeons using next-gen robotics in cardiac, neuro & orthopaedic

Premium Care:Deliver deeply personalised, patient-centred care in a 100% private-room en-suite facility

Safe Staffing: Work with peace of mind under an historic EA delivering mandated nurse-to-patient ratios

Professional Growth: Accelerate your career with clinical education programs & funded postgrad pathways

Health & Wellbeing: Fitness Passport, discounted private health, & cultural recognitions and celebrations

Sponsorship - work rights for Australia

Please note, visa sponsorship is not available for this position. For this role you must be an Australian or New Zealand citizen or have an Australia visa that grants you the work rights necessary for the role.

Equal opportunity

We celebrate diversity & inclusion and are committed to equal employment opportunity for everyone.

As part of our commitment to reconciliation, we encourage Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples to apply and join us in delivering care that heals body, mind, spirit and community.

How to apply

The closing date for applications is 16th August 2026. Shortlisting for this position will commence immediately. We encourage you to apply promptly as the advertisement may close early should a suitable applicant be sourced.

Please submit your resume. A cover letter is welcome but not required.

Respectfully, this role is not open to recruitment agencies.
